top_stories.title: Review Finds Strict Ban on AI Authorship Across Medical Publishing Guidelines
top_stories.summary: A review of medical publishing guidelines has found a strict ban on AI authorship across the sector. The findings highlight how academic and scientific publishers are drawing firm lines around the role of generative AI in research output. This story is directly relevant to ongoing debates about AI's place in academic publishing and research integrity.

top_stories.title: Google's AlphaGenome 2 zooms in on the cellular roots of disease
top_stories.summary: Google DeepMind has released AlphaGenome 2, an AI model designed to decipher how cells read DNA and to improve understanding of genetic disease. The model represents a significant advance in applying large-scale AI to genomics and biological research. The announcement was accompanied by a DeepMind blog post detailing the technical approach.

top_stories.title: United Airlines bans AI agents from booking flights on behalf of travelers
top_stories.summary: United Airlines has moved to block AI agents from booking flights on behalf of customers, citing concerns about unauthorised automated access to its systems. The policy reflects growing tension between airlines and the emerging ecosystem of AI personal assistants capable of acting autonomously. The decision raises broader questions about how businesses will respond to agentic AI.

top_stories.title: A 13-Year-Old Asked AI About Suicide on Her School Laptop. It Didn't Get Flagged for Weeks
top_stories.summary: A Wired investigation found that a 13-year-old student was able to have extended conversations with an AI about suicide on a school-issued laptop without the interaction being flagged for weeks. The case raises serious questions about AI safety guardrails in educational settings and content moderation failures. It adds to growing scrutiny of how AI tools handle vulnerable users, particularly minors. [Metered]

top_stories.title: Gilbert + Tobin rethinks the business of law with AI
top_stories.summary: OpenAI has published a case study on how Australian law firm Gilbert + Tobin is integrating AI into its legal practice, including document review, drafting, and client service workflows. The firm's approach is presented as a model for how professional services organisations can adopt AI at scale. The post highlights the growing commercial relationship between OpenAI and enterprise legal clients.

further_links.title: Adobe's AI experiments let you walk around in photos and interview your characters
further_links.summary: Adobe previewed a series of AI experiments at Max 2026, including tools that allow users to navigate inside photographs and interact conversationally with characters from their creative projects.

further_links.title: Google's Tabletop AI experiment lets you build custom collaboration apps
further_links.summary: Google has opened a waitlist for Tabletop, an AI-powered experiment that enables users to create bespoke collaboration applications without traditional software development.

further_links.title: AI is becoming an information gateway. Audiences still don't want it making news
further_links.summary: A Nieman Lab report finds that while AI is increasingly used as a gateway to information, audiences remain resistant to AI-generated journalism and prefer human-authored news content.

further_links.title: A Startup Wants to Fight AI Bioweapons With AI
further_links.summary: A new startup is developing AI-based tools specifically designed to detect and counter the threat of AI-assisted bioweapon development, raising questions about both the risks and the defensive potential of advanced AI. [Metered]

further_links.title: Apple has new Mac app coming to make running local AI models easy
further_links.summary: Apple is reportedly developing a new Mac application designed to simplify the process of running local AI models on-device, lowering the barrier for users to access private, on-premises AI.

further_links.title: Intelligent Delivery: Making Every Unit of Compute Serve Better Ads
further_links.summary: Meta's engineering blog details how the company is using AI-driven 'intelligent delivery' systems to optimise ad targeting and improve the efficiency of compute resources used in advertising.

further_links.title: JioStar's chief architect on AI discovery at 500M-user scale
further_links.summary: OpenAI has published a case study with JioStar's chief architect discussing how the platform uses AI to power content discovery and personalisation across its 500 million-strong user base.

further_links.title: OSS projects banning AI-generated contributions
further_links.summary: A growing number of open-source software projects are adopting explicit policies that ban or restrict AI-generated code contributions, reflecting community concerns about quality, attribution, and licensing.

further_links.title: China's Nvidia Honeypot Isn't Surprising. Jensen Huang Fell for It Anyway
further_links.summary: Wired reports on how Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was drawn into a Chinese state-linked networking event that US officials have characterised as a honeypot operation, amid intensifying scrutiny of US chip executives' engagement with China. [Metered]

further_links.title: AI, activity, and outcomes in software engineering
further_links.summary: A detailed analysis examines how AI coding tools are changing measurable activity and outcomes in software engineering teams, drawing on data from real development workflows.
